item.title: Said & Checked, Arkansas, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 7 unsettled (Bruce Westerman, Melanie Stansbury)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Bruce Westerman, U.S. Representative from Arkansas: “In the late 19th century, North America's buffalo population fell from tens of millions to approximately 1,000.” Unsettled. Published estimates put the pre-1800 population at 30 to 60 million, which fits 'tens of millions', but give the low point variously as 325 (1884), 541 (U.S., 1889), about 300 (1900) or about 1,000. 'Approximately 1,000' fits some counts and not others. Figures are as compiled by Wikipedia; no primary count was read.
  • Bruce Westerman, U.S. Representative from Arkansas: “Originally, the Tribe's reservation spanned over 15,000 acres until the city of San Diego initiated a land sale in 1931 so it could build the El Capitan Reservoir.” Unsettled. The Capitan Grande Reservation covered 15,753 acres, which matches 'over 15,000 acres', and the El Capitan Reservoir flooded its core in 1931 (as compiled by Wikipedia). A summary of a UC Irvine article cites purchase acts of 1919 and 1932, so the year the sale began is not confirmed.
  • Melanie Stansbury, U.S. Representative from New Mexico: “The Crossett Experimental Forest was established in 1933” Unsettled. The Encyclopedia of Arkansas gives the forest's boundary as laid out in October 1933 and says it was 'established in 1934', with the deed conveyed Aug. 2, 1934. No official Forest Service establishment date was read, so 1933 fits one reading and not the other.

item.title: Said & Checked, Arkansas, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 2 unsupported, 9 unsettled (Sean Duffy)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “Reported as: In a post on the social media platform X, Duffy said contractor L3Harris Technologies Inc. had secured two routers from FAA facilities in Texas and Arkansas and was conducting "deep diagnostics" on the equipment.” Unsupported. The FAA names two sites, in Amarillo, Texas and El Dorado, Arkansas, and a new router at El Dorado, and says it and L3Harris are still investigating. Neither the FAA nor L3Harris says two routers were secured or that diagnostics are under way; the only source found for that is the secretary's post.
  • Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “Now, we know who did the install. A good American patriot, we believe, a veteran.” Unsupported. No public record identifying the installer, or describing the installer as a veteran, was found. The search covered the FAA's published Q&A, a CNBC report and web searches on the installer; an Arkansas newspaper article could not be read.
  • Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “So we were forced by the telecom provider to actually update that copper to fiber, and we brought in our routers and did the work.” Unsettled. The FAA's published Q&A says copper wires are "being disconnected due to their obsolescence" in this type of work. It does not say the telecom provider retired the El Dorado line or required the move to fiber there. The Transportation Department's Nov. 14 briefing page could not be read.

Contradictions

  • Contradicts own statement.
    Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “So we were forced by the telecom provider to actually update that copper to fiber, and we brought in our routers and did the work.” (unsettled)
    Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “There was an old fiber line that was going to be decommissioned by our telecom provider.” (unsettled)
    Both statements in context
